A total of 1,339 vessel calls were recorded during the period. Containerised cargo dominated operations at 52% of total commercial cargo movement, followed by mineral bulk at 36 percent, with the remaining 12% comprising vehicles, general cargo, other fluids and agricultural bulk. Container throughput reached 2,007,493 TEUs, a 3% increase compared to the same period in 2025. candidates.title: Port of Los Angeles records lowest emissions per container
candidates.excerpt: The Port of Los Angeles has released its 2025 Inventory of Air Emissions, recording its lowest emissions per container on record and continuing a two-decade trend of significant reductions alongside growing cargo volumes. In 2025, the port handled nearly 10.2 million TEUs while achieving year-on-year declines across all major pollutants: diesel particulate matter fell 2%, nitrogen oxides declined 4%, sulfur oxides dropped 5% and greenhouse gases decreased 3% compared to 2024. The NOx reduction marked the lowest annual total for that pollutant since the port began tracking emissions in 2005. Since 2005, the port has reduced DPM by 90 percent, NOx by 72 percent, SOx by 98 percent and GHGs by 16%, while container volumes have increased 37%. Since the 2017 update to the Clean Air Action Plan, DPM, NOx, SOx and GHGs are down 15 percent, 38 percent, 28% and 9% respectively. candidates.excerpt: Ontario Midland Railroad has secured an $11.2 million federal grant to rehabilitate approximately 10 miles of track in Wayne County, New York, improving infrastructure that supports the region’s agricultural and manufacturing shippers. The Wayne County Mainline Safety and Reliability Project will replace approximately nine miles of rail, resurface eight grade crossings, replace seven turnouts and remove three others. Work also includes ballast placement, tamping and track surfacing, according to an Oct. 19 announcement from the railroad and U.S. Sens. Chuck Schumer and Kirsten Gillibrand. The award comes through the Federal Railroad Administration’s Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements, or CRISI, program. candidates.title: Union Pacific CFO to retire
candidates.excerpt: Chief Financial Officer Jennifer Hamann will retire in early 2027, Union Pacific (NYSE: UNP) has announced. Hamann, who joined Union Pacific in 1992, was named CFO in January 2020. She had previously held leadership roles in a broad range of areas, including finance, human resources, marketing and sales, investor relations, and corporate audit. “For 35 years, she led with integrity and heart, guiding our finances through historic challenges, executing our strategy, mentoring future leaders and representing Union Pacific across the industry,” UP Chief Executive Jim Vena said in release. “Jennifer was tough — she never said yes unless she believed it was the right thing to do for Union Pacific. She made this railroad stronger, and her contributions will be felt for generations. I am deeply grateful for her leadership and friendship.” Hamann is the first woman to serve as the railroad’s chief financial officer. candidates.excerpt: Intramotev will deploy two autonomous freight railcars on Missouri’s Columbia Terminal Railroad as part of a project supported by a $16.2 million federal grant awarded to the City of Columbia.
